transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (CTO, Hygeia), Liam O'Connor (Head of IT), Tara Benson (Security Engineer)

Summary (auto):
Quick security posture discovery for hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Focus on SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention and regulatory constraints. Customer interested in Private or Dedicated for PHI use cases; exploring Hosted for non-PII workloads.

Topics: SOC2, ISO 27001, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, VPC/private deployments, data retention/residency, pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Maya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Dr. Priya Rao: Good thanks. Quick note we have to keep this high level, some of the compliance folks are out but Tara's here who handles our security controls.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Yep, thanks. We're evaluating a few vendors for inference 
 d main thing is PHI handling and auditability.
[00:27] Maya Singh: Great, can I ask a bit about your current stack? Where do you host your models today, and what kind of data classification are we talking about?
[00:36] Tara Benson: We run a mix 
 internal models on-prem for PII/PHI, some ML workloads on clouds for non-sensitive data. The use case for Redwood would be triage/summarization of patient intake notes, so definitely PHI in scope.
[00:52] Alex Chen: Understood. From a Redwood perspective we offer Hosted, Dedicated, and Private 
 hosted is easiest but not suitable for PHI with current controls unless you use tokenization/pseudonymization. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and stronger isolation; Private gives you a VPC/on-prem control plane with KMS integrations.
[01:15] Dr. Priya Rao: Can you clarify the difference in encryption key management between Dedicated and Private? Is KMS customer-managed?
[01:23] Maya Singh: Yeah so for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS for disk and object encryption in many setups but the control plane is still Redwood-managed. For Private, the control plane can be customer-hosted or we provide configs to connect to their HSM/KMS 
 customer holds keys, we support bring-your-own-key flows, rotation, and audit hooks.
[01:44] Liam O'Connor: We need proof of that 
 like diagrams and the exact KMS integrations, supported HSM vendors, OKTA SAML flows, and audit log retention periods.
[01:52] Alex Chen: Absolutely, we'll send architecture diagrams and the KMS/HSM matrix. We'll also include our SAML guide for Okta and Azure AD.
[02:01] Tara Benson: Another thing 
 SOC 2 and ISO. We are required to review SOC 2 Type II. Do you have that available?
[02:06] Alex Chen: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 scope doc. I can share those under NDA; we'll attach the latest reports and our security whitepaper.
[02:15] Dr. Priya Rao: NDA will be fine. Also how granular is your RBAC? We need team-level isolation, least-privilege for engineers vs ops, and audit trails for token usage.
[02:25] Maya Singh: RBAC is role-based and can map to SAML groups. You can define roles at org, project, and route level. We also log token usage, per-route request/response metadata and return audit events to your logging endpoint or SIEM.
[02:41] Liam O'Connor: Is the audit log immutable and how long do you retain them? We have e-discovery needs for 7 years for some datasets.
[02:49] Maya Singh: Default retention on Hosted is 90 days, Dedicated can be configured longer, and with Private you control retention entirely. For long-term retention, we stream logs to S3 or a customer SIEM 
 we can support immutable WORM storage if needed through your cloud provider.
[03:05] Tara Benson: Ok that helps. What about redaction and data minimization? We can't keep full payloads of patient text in logs.
[03:11] Maya Singh: We support configurable scrubbers and redaction rules. For Hosted we offer out-of-the-box redaction and configurable hashing/pseudonymization prior to storage. For Private, you can implement pre-ingest transformers in your network.
[03:26] Speaker 1: (mumble) how about endpoint security, certs, mTLS?
[03:31] Alex Chen: We support mTLS for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports TLS; mTLS can be enabled for Dedicated customers upon request.
[03:38] Dr. Priya Rao: Any third-party pen testing or bug bounty?
[03:42] Alex Chen: Yes, we do annual pen tests and run a continuous vulnerability scanning program; we also have a public responsible disclosure policy. We'll include the pen test summary and SCA (software composition analysis) high-level findings.
[03:55] Liam O'Connor: On identity 
 we use Okta. We want SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Is SCIM supported?
[04:02] Maya Singh: Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for user/group sync, and SAML SSO for auth. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. We'll share the SAML metadata and an Okta quickstart.
[04:13] Tara Benson: For compliance, does Redwood provide evidence for control mappings to HIPAA controls?
[04:19] Alex Chen: We have a compliance matrix that maps SOC 2 controls to HIPAA and other frameworks as well as our internal policies. We'll share that matrix.
[04:27] Dr. Priya Rao: Great. From a timeline perspective, if we want to pilot in dedicated or private for PHI workflows, what does onboarding look like? How long to get up?
[04:36] Maya Singh: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 2-4 weeks for basic setup and testing, Private (VPC) can be 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS/HSM procurement. For PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer KMS, plus a short validation run with synthetic data.
[04:53] Alex Chen: We can also do a hybrid: host non-PII workloads on Hosted while you ramp up Dedicated/Private for PHI. Many customers do that to get value quickly.
[05:02] Liam O'Connor: Cost vs latency tradeoffs: if we go Private on-prem, what's the expected latency hit vs Hosted?
[05:08] Maya Singh: On-prem can be lower latency if close to your apps, but you control the hardware. Hosted will have predictable global endpoints; Dedicated gives capacity guarantees. We can run an initial benchmark to show p50/p95 token latencies.
[05:21] Tara Benson: Benchmarks 
 we want to see p95 for 512 tokens and for streaming chat. Also need sample throughput numbers for reserved capacity.
[05:29] Maya Singh: We'll include a benchmark template and runbook. For Dedicated we provide throughput guarantees in the reserved capacity contract.
[05:36] Dr. Priya Rao: About data residency 
 we operate in US and EU. Some PHI must stay in US-only regions. Can you ensure region pinning?
[05:45] Alex Chen: Yes, we support region pinning for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region routing; Dedicated/Private can be pinned to specific cloud regions and you can require that data not cross regions.
[05:56] Speaker 2: what about deletion and retention APIs?
[05:59] Maya Singh: We provide retention policies and deletion APIs for customer data. For Hosted, deletion is supported but you should confirm downstream backups; for Private you fully control deletion. We'll document retention endpoints.
[06:10] Tara Benson: Do you support isolation for PII at rest, e.g., separate keys per customer or per-tenant encryption?
[06:16] Maya Singh: Yes, per-customer keys are supported and per-tenant keying can be done on Private. For Dedicated we can do per-customer KMS keys, dependent on cloud provider features.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: Legal/procurement note: we'll need SLAs for uptime and incident response. Any SOC2 incident reporting cadence?
[06:34] Alex Chen: We have incident response SLA tiers and we commit to notify customers according to contractual terms; standard is 72-hour breach notification plus faster escalation for critical incidents. We can add tighter terms for enterprise contracts.
[06:48] Dr. Priya Rao: On logging 
 can logs be pushed to our SIEM in near real-time and include request-response hashes, user IDs, and token metadata?
[06:56] Maya Singh: Yes, logs can stream to your SIEM via Kinesis/Cloud Pub/Sub or syslog; we include metadata but redact full payloads by default unless you enable it.
[07:06] Tara Benson: We need to ensure that archived logs do not store cleartext patient content 
 how is payload redaction enforced at rest?
[07:12] Maya Singh: Redaction is a pipeline stage prior to log storage. For Hosted, we offer managed redaction. For Dedicated/Private, you can add filters in the ingestion layer. We'll provide config snippets.
[07:23] Alex Chen: Quick qual question 
 what's your procurement timeline and who's the final approver?
[07:28] Dr. Priya Rao: Procurement starts next quarter, legal and security will gate. CFO signs off on spend over $250k. We're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q2.
[07:38] Alex Chen: Good to know. We'll aim to get the security artifacts over quickly.
[07:41] Speaker 3: (crosstalk) any questions on data residency?
[07:45] Liam O'Connor: One more 
 do you have ar-chive retention controls for 7yrs and can WORM be enforced?
[07:51] Maya Singh: Yes via customer cloud storage and lifecycle rules you can enforce WORM and retention. We'll include guidance for S3 WORM or equivalent.
[08:00] Dr. Priya Rao: Ok let's talk about a POC scope. If we do a POC for PHI triage, what's realistic?
[08:08] Maya Singh: POC typically 4 weeks: week 1 - set up Dedicated environment and SAML, week 2 - ingest synthetic dataset and run test prompts, week 3 - evaluate quality and tweak redaction, week 4 - run a performance benchmark and handoff doc.
[08:22] Tara Benson: We'll need to run a compliance checklist during POC and have your SE present for the infra runbook.
[08:28] Maya Singh: Totally 
 SE will lead infra runbook and validation.
[08:31] Alex Chen: Recap of immediate deliverables: SOC2 Type II, architecture/KMS matrix, SAML quickstart, RBAC examples, benchmark template, and draft POC scope with pricing.
[08:44] Dr. Priya Rao: Sounds good. Please include any limitations of Hosted for PHI so procurement understands the constraints.
[08:50] Alex Chen: We'll call that out explicitly.
[08:53] Liam O'Connor: For follow-up, can you also provide names for customer references in healthcare?
[08:58] Alex Chen: We can share anonymized references and case studies; we'll ensure approvals.
[09:05] Speaker 1: (minor hesitation) how often do you rotate keys?
[09:09] Maya Singh: Key rotation is configurable; we recommend 90-day rotations for customer-managed keys but support custom schedules.
[09:15] Dr. Priya Rao: Ok I'm going to hand off to Tara for a deeper technical questionnaire offline.
[09:20] Tara Benson: Great. A couple of quick clarifications: do you keep raw model outputs anywhere for Hosted?
[09:26] Alex Chen: By default Hosted retains short-term traces for debugging up to 90 days; we can publish options to disable retention for specific routes. For Dedicated and Private you control retention.|
[09:40] Liam O'Connor: We'll want to disable retention for PHI routes.
[09:43] Maya Singh: That's supported 
 policy-based route settings allow you to disable persistence.
[09:49] Dr. Priya Rao: Anything else from Redwood?
[09:52] Alex Chen: Nothing else. We'll send the docs and propose a technical deep dive next week.
[09:58] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks all.

End notes (auto):
Call ended with clear next steps and agreement to exchange security artifacts. Suitable candidate for Dedicated/Private pilot for PHI; Hosted viable for non-PII workloads only.

References/links mentioned: SOC2 Type II (will share), SAML/SSO guide (Okta quickstart), KMS/HSM support matrix (will share), benchmark template (will share).
